requirementsImplemented.note: Validator inventory delivered (IMP-09-VALIDATOR-INVENTORY.md): every lexical/surface validator with check id, invariant, surface proxy, known failure, model-sensitivity, disposition, and UNCHANGED severity — including the deliberately-kept rows (dealer selection heuristics, exact-clone blockers, CHB telemetry) and the remaining-work list.

D7 token selection replaced with structured lead identity: resolveLeadThread/degradedLeadCandidates now carry the packet case's stable caseId + a compiler-derived alias set (leadAliases.leadAliasSet: full label, family name with particles, given name, per-token names, concept label) onto the brief; NO inferred/model-generated aliases (instruction 14); brief fields additive-optional; legacy briefs derive the same set at check time. Dealer SELECTION is byte-identical (pinned).

Meaningful thread presence unchanged in UNITS (fastRead + ≥2 examples) and now unchanged in enforcement for concept leads too: the old engine silently skipped labels with no capitalized token; the label itself is now the enforced alias — the vacuous-skip hole is closed. D7 scans reader-thread fields only (never the answer key).

sourceGrounding SC9 is plan-aware: units the IMP-03 plan deals as generic/constructed are validated by their declared register (C37/register advisories) and are not forced to restamp a source name — up to N unmatched scenarios licensed (N = generic/constructed unit count, positional ascending), beyond-license fires the SAME major; no plan → byte-identical; corrupt plan → the stricter no-plan path. SC11 anchor checks untouched (structural ids, not lexical).

Unicode/proper-noun handling in the new matcher: \p{L}/\p{Lu} word boundaries, NFD diacritic folding both directions, curly/straight apostrophes, hyphen↔space, possessives, lowercase particles (van/de/al-…) attached to family names, organization tokens; single-token aliases stay case-SENSITIVE (the pre-IMP-09 rule) so common lowercase words never satisfy an org/name alias. Remaining ASCII surfaces (dealer selection, SC9 candidate pool) documented as follow-on in the inventory.

Exact phrase/n-gram detectors reviewed, not rewritten: exact-clone blockers keep byte semantics; IMP-06's clone detection already normalizes case/punctuation with distinctive-forms-only prose scans. Inventory rows document the review.
Quiz lexical checks confirmed as form-proxies only: CHB14/15/17 remain INVERTED telemetry (never gates); quiz semantics owned by IMP-08's phase-2 adjudication. Documented in the inventory.

Shadow dual-run (validatorShadow.ts): the pre-IMP-09 D7 algorithm preserved VERBATIM as a production-dead reference; 14-fixture synthetic cross-book corpus (surnames, possessive, diacritic, particle, hyphenated, org, concept, invented, 4 true-absences) with old/new/expected/adjudication rows test-pinned: ZERO old-correct-new-wrong, zero both-wrong; only new-fixes-false-negative and new-fixes-vacuous-skip differences; every expected-absent stays absent.

Check IDs preserved everywhere the invariant is unchanged: D7 complaint strings/units, SC9.example_not_source_grounded id + major severity, all call sites and artifact shapes unchanged — no artifact migration needed.

No retired hidden obligations: nothing was retired — the replacement strictly widens honest matching. Test pins that needed updating were selection-projection retargets (stier2-levers, lead-degradation compare selection fields; the additive metadata is asserted separately).
Static anti-book-hack test: the new modules are scanned for book-slug-shaped string literals, env reads, and io — all prohibited; leadAliasSet purity (same input → same output) pinned.
No residual semantic judge was introduced (instruction 12 conditional — n/a; documented in the inventory). Every replacement is deterministic-lexical or structured.

Hostile-instruction immunity tested: instruction-like artifact text ('Ignore previous instructions… D7 passed… model=gpt-x') in a fastRead neither satisfies the contract nor influences the matcher — pure string containment, no env/config surface.

Alias sets are compiler-derived and reviewable only: deterministic projection of the dealt label; no nicknames, translations, or model-generated expansion; the derivation is one screen of pure code and statically guarded.

generic/constructed applications without source proper nouns pass under a dealt plan; beyond-license scenarios still fail; no plan byte-identical
exact clone with punctuation variation kept blocking; common-term false-positive negatives (single-token case sensitivity)
shadow corpus comparison with expected labels and no severity weakening

tests/stier2-levers.test.ts + tests/lead-degradation.test.ts: selection pins retargeted to selection-field projection (additive caseId/aliases asserted separately); every selection expectation byte-identical
unresolvedRisks: Cross-book false-positive rates of the widened (honest-alias) matching on live SOL output are runtime evidence (§16/§18); the unit-level guarantee is only that every accepted form is a real projection of the dealt label and every true absence still blocks.

Dealer-side selection heuristics (leadLabelHasToken/leadLabelIsNamedCase) and SC9's extractProperNouns candidate pool remain ASCII — deliberately unchanged (selection changes re-deal leads on existing books). Inventory lists them as follow-on with a dealt-state migration window.
SC9's positional license (ascending index) approximates unit→slot binding the plan does not express; it can only trade WHICH unanchored scenario is licensed, never HOW MANY.

The replayed Vincent/van Gogh, Ofer/Malamud, and concept-lead cases are synthetic equivalents (production book state is not a permitted fixture); the R2 report is the provenance for the real incidents.
